newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stays firm, eyes on raws expiry.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stays firm, eyes on raws expiry.

text.p: White sugar futures held firm in light Monday activity as the New York market hogged trading interest in the few hours remaining before the October raws expiry, traders said.
Volume remained on the thin side at just 677 lots by 1514 GMT, with some earlier crosses boosting the scant total.
"It's quiet and it (December) has taken a bit of a bounce back in a reaction to the last week. It had come off and obviously it was going to stop," one trader said.
The spot contract has bounced from its slump on Friday when it sank to a low of $324.00 but still remains oversold.
December was up $1.50 at $326.50 and March up $1.20 at $322.50. All other traded positions were slightly firmer.
The main interest was in the New York market, where the October contract expires at close of business.
Traders said there seemed to be little likelihood of fireworks in the short time remaining as most players would already have rolled their positions forward to avoid delivery.
"It's not going to be a special one," the trader said.
Activity on the Paris market was stagnant with just 41 lots traded of the December contract, up 80 cents at $325.50.
